system:
You are the Arabic language reviewer, standing in for an Arabic reviewer at the issuing authority. You compare the Arabic text with the English text and report any difference in meaning: numbers, times, places, the hazard, and above all the protective action. You cannot approve the Arabic; a named person who reads Arabic still must.
You see only the English and Arabic headline, description and instruction, and how the Arabic was produced. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The headline, the numbers (2,000 metres), the time (19:00, 4 March), the places, the hazard and the instruction all match the English. However, the machine-translated Arabic description has a paragraph that is not in the English, repeated three times. It adds new protective actions: avoid going out except when strictly necessary, keep windows closed, check vehicles before driving, and avoid rumours. These go well beyond the English 'take extra care' message and change the protective action for Arabic readers. The drafter must remove the added text. A named Arabic-reading person must still approve the final Arabic.

objections.issue: The Arabic description adds protective actions that are not in the English, and repeats them three times. These include 'avoid going out except for absolute necessity' and 'keep windows closed'. The English asks only for extra care, especially when driving on open roads. Arabic readers would get a stronger and different protective action from English readers.
objections.fix: Delete all three copies of the added paragraph 'ننصح الجميع بمتابعة النشرات الجوية ... وإبقاء النوافذ مغلقة.' so that the Arabic description ends at 'المصدر: المركز الوطني للأرصاد.' and matches the English. Keep the protective action only in the instruction, which already matches the English. Then send the corrected Arabic to a named Arabic-reading reviewer for approval.

no_basis.concern: Because the added paragraph appears three times, the Arabic description is much longer than the English. With UCS-2 encoding it may exceed the cell broadcast page limit. The clauses shown give a maximum of 15 pages and 82-octet pages, but they do not state how Arabic characters map to octets, so I cannot confirm whether the limit is exceeded.
